image_description: A close-up, low-light photograph of a dark wooden bookcase. The left side shows shelves containing books (some with colorful spines), a small box, and a white object on the bottom shelf. To the right, there is a large cardboard box with graphics sitting on the floor next to the bookcase, and a blue curved surface (possibly a chair or wall) in the background. The lighting is dim and warm, casting shadows.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular furniture piece of considerable height, notably taller than wide.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the furniture extends vertically beyond the frame, implying significant height. The width of the visible section is narrower than its implied height, consistent with a tall bookcase.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tall rectangular frame with horizontal divisions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Clear horizontal shelf lines are visible, dividing the vertical space into compartments. The structure appears rectangular.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with open front displaying books and objects.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped asymmetrically, showing only the left edge/corner of the bookcase. Full bilateral symmetry cannot be verified due to occlusion/cropping.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Multiple horizontal shelves spaced evenly from top to bottom.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: At least three distinct shelf levels are visible within the frame, holding items. Spacing appears consistent.
Adjustability is an internal mechanical feature (pins/holes) not clearly visible in this low-resolution, shadowed image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some models have glass doors on upper section.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No glass doors are visible in the current view; the front appears open.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood particleboard or metal with finished surface stained painted or laminated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture and color suggest dark-stained wood or laminate. Reflections indicate a finished surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Front open displaying books and objects on each shelf.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Books and miscellaneous objects are clearly visible on the shelves, and there are no doors obstructing the view.
No decorative hardware (knobs, handles) is visible. The surface is finished, but the 'decorative hardware' part of the checkpoint is not met.

artifact_observations.location: entire image, especially edges of books and box
artifact_observations.reasoning: Significant softness and lack of sharp detail throughout the image, likely due to low light/high ISO noise reduction or camera shake. Edges of books bleed slightly into backgrounds.
The graphics on the box appear slightly smeared and lack crisp text definition, typical of AI generation or heavy compression, but hard to distinguish from motion blur.

artifact_observations.location: right side boundary between bookcase and background
artifact_observations.reasoning: The vertical line of the bookcase seems to waver slightly against the dark background, possibly indicating minor geometric instability or blending issues.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the primary object is indeed a bookcase and not a similar shelving unit or cabinet.
To assess the severity of blur and noise, distinguishing between photographic artifacts and AI generation artifacts.
To verify that shelves are structurally connected to the side panels and do not float or merge incorrectly.
To identify if the objects on shelves are coherent 'books' or nonsensical shapes, and to segment the box for boundary checking.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of shelf connections to vertical supports
Coherence of book spines (text/logos vs gibberish)
Boundary sharpness between bookcase and dark background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'books' on the shelf. In AI images, these often melt into each other or have gibberish text. Also, check if the vertical support of the bookcase actually connects to the shelves or if it floats. The low light makes this tricky; differentiate between noise/blur and structural melting.
